description: The Open DS grammar: a finite set of questions a design system must answer. Reasons come first (business, people, content, tasks, human factors, outcomes, brand, use scenarios, team). Scopes follow, from typography to voice and tone. Every scope answers the same five method questions (roles, how many, how defined, values, lands in) and has the same parts: the tokens it owns, the components it lands in and its situations. Each scheme answers every question, and each answer says why and which earlier answers it follows from. Situations are the moments where people need to know what to use; each scheme answers them too. Component keys are the shared component API every scheme fills.

scheme_order.why: The first three are shaped by what people do: scan and compare, read, finish the task. The last two are shaped by the brand: one loud brand, then many brands as themes, the most involved. Dense data comes first; it is the default everywhere.

ai.use_when: You need the list of questions behind a design system, or the meaning of a question id such as typography.definition or a situation id such as number-in-table.
ai.how_to_read: Reasons are answered first. A scope answer lists in 'because' the answers that pulled it. Scope question ids are <scope>.<method>, so typography.values and voice.values answer the same kind of question. Tokens follow from the answers. Components read only component keys. Written text in a scheme (voice, scenarios) lists in 'follows' the answers it was written from.

layers.description: Why the system exists: product, people, content, tasks, human factors, outcomes, brand, use scenarios, team.
The design decisions: typography, color, spacing, shape, elevation, motion, iconography, theming, accessibility, naming, voice and tone, components. Each answers the five method questions.
Primitives are the options; each option looks clearly different from the others (see options). Semantics are the decisions, in light and dark. Brands and modes are themes.
One key per component element, variant and state. Every scheme fills every key.

options.description: Rules every scheme's primitives follow (OD-221, OD-222). An option set exists to offer distinct choices, so each option looks clearly different from the others: two steps you cannot tell apart are one step. Prefer fewer steps that each do a job over one step per role. And keep only the options something reads: an option nothing reads is a choice nobody made.

used.say: outside color ramps, keep only the options a semantic, theme or component key reads
used.why: An option nothing reads is a choice nobody made. Color ramps stay whole, because a ramp is one unit with meaning.

rules.say: line heights are ratios of the text size, at least 0.2 apart
rules.why: A ratio follows each text's own size, and steps closer than 0.2 look the same.

hints.do: A scale is one color in steps, from lightened (50) to darkened (950). The steps are made in OKLCH, a color space built around how the eye sees lightness, and each step mostly moves the color's lightness. The steps aren't evenly spaced in lightness: at the light and dark ends they are tweaked so that each gap means the same, one step more of use. The light tints sit close together, so there is a choice of soft backgrounds; the middle steps step out as fills, borders and buttons; the dark end gives strong text. Colorfulness eases toward the ends. Each scale starts from its own key color at 600 and keeps that hue's natural lightness and contrast: a yellow is light by nature and a blue is dark, so their steps sit around where each hue really is, not at the same values for every hue. So every step still reads as the same color.
hints.why: When every step is one step of use, people can pick the right strength for each job, and the screen stays calm and consistent.

hints.when: You pick a step for something.
hints.do: Use the lightest steps for backgrounds behind text, the middle steps for buttons, borders and focus rings, and the darkest steps for text on light backgrounds. In dark mode the roles swap ends.
hints.why: Text must stand out from what is behind it. Each end of the scale gives that for the other end.

hints.when: A step looks wrong where it is used.
hints.do: Say exactly what is wrong first: too pale, too dull, too close to another color. Then change only that step, and leave the ones that work alone.
hints.measure: The harness checks that every step that was changed really needed it.
hints.why: A small fix in the right place keeps the family together. Reworking a whole scale for one problem makes new problems.

hints.do: Find everything that uses it, and look at each one in light and dark mode. One step can be a soft background in light mode and a text color in dark mode at the same time.
hints.why: A change made for one use moves every other use of that step too.

hints.when: A step looks washed out or greyish.
hints.do: OKLCH gives a step three dials: lightness, colorfulness and hue. Turn colorfulness first. If that is not enough, make it a little darker. Turn the hue last.
hints.why: Darkening a pale color makes it grayer, not more colorful. How colorful it is decides whether people recognize it.

hints.when: You make a very pale step more colorful.
hints.do: Expect blue and red to need a touch of darkening before they can take more color. Green and yellow usually take it as they are.
hints.why: Screens can show only so much color in very pale steps, and blue and red run out of room first.

hints.when: Text is set in a color, like an error message or a status label.
hints.do: Make sure it is easy to read and also clearly that color. Text that is readable but looks white has lost its meaning.
hints.measure: The harness checks that status text on dark backgrounds is clearly colored and easy to read, in every scheme.
hints.why: The color tells people what kind of message it is before they read a word.

hints.when: You decide how much to change.
hints.do: Change as little as solves the problem. Then compare it with the original side by side, in light and dark mode, and ease it back if it stands out.
hints.why: A big change makes the step look like it belongs to another color.

hints.when: The same problem shows up in several schemes.
hints.do: If the schemes use the same color, fix it once for all of them. Fix one scheme alone only when its color is different.
hints.why: The same blue is the same color wherever it is used, so it has the same problem everywhere.

hints.when: Every color seems to need the same fix.
hints.do: Change how all the scales are made, instead of fixing each color one by one.
hints.why: A fix is for an exception. When every color needs it, the rule itself is what needs to change.

hints.do: Write down why, in a sentence anyone can follow. "It looked too pale on dark backgrounds" is a good reason.
hints.why: Whoever comes next can keep the change, adjust it, or undo it on purpose.

hints.when: Two colors must never be confused, like the main button and a delete button.
hints.do: Decide how different they must be from where they appear together, not from one number for every case.
hints.why: Colors side by side need more difference than colors that never meet.

questions.text: Which spacing roles does it need?
questions.description: The groups of space decisions.

How big the steps between spaces are. Small steps on a 4px grid suit dense screens and shared forms; big, even steps suit reading and big moments.

hints.do: Never write a spacing as a number: not p-6, not gap-1.5, not p-[10px]. Every spacing has a name. Between things and on the page, use a role: gap-tight, gap-default, gap-group, gap-section, p-container, px-control, px-cell. Inside a component of your own, use a step of the component spacing map: gap-map-x2, p-map-x6.
hints.why: A number looks right in one scheme and wrong in the next. A name follows the scheme, so the screen keeps its density in every scheme.

hints.when: When you space the inside of a component.
hints.do: The component spacing map is the steps components space by. Each step is 4px × its multiplier (x1, x2, x3, x4, x6, x8, x12) × the scheme's rhythm, rounded to a multiple of 4px, at most 64px. A compact scheme has rhythm 1 and a spacious one up to 2, so a dialog's padding (x6) is 24px in one and 48px in the other. The scheme decides which steps hold still: x1 and x2 are the fine spacing inside rows, so lists stay lists in a roomy scheme. The hairline is a fixed 2px nudge. Pick the step nearest the space you want.
hints.why: One unit keeps everything on one grid; the rhythm lets each scheme decide how roomy its components are.

hints.when: When one component looks too tight or too loose.
hints.do: Don't change the rhythm to fix one component. The rhythm is the whole scheme's density. Pick another step for that spacing instead, or ask for a new role if the same spacing repeats across components.
hints.why: A rhythm change moves every component in the scheme at once.

semantics.description: What each semantic key is for, written once for every scheme. Each entry says its intent, what to use it for, what not to use it for (and what to use instead) and, where it matters, which fills it may sit on and the contrast it must keep there. Words only; values come from each scheme. The harness checks every rule.

urgency.description: Status colors go up in urgency: info, then warning, then danger. Pick the level that matches the real risk. Never go up a level to get attention. Success sits outside the order.

The label on a dark danger fill, such as its tint in dark mode: a fixed color from the light scale (100, adjusted so its hue shows).

tones.description: Text pairs with fills by tone (OD-222, OD-227). Every fill states its tone, light or dark, in each brand and mode: a decision, written on the fill as $extensions.open-ds.tone. Two text tokens serve every fill: color.text.on-light (the light mode's body text) on a light fill, color.text.on-dark (white) on a dark one, the same in both modes. Per-fill names (color.text.inverse, color.text.on-action, color.text.on-danger) point at the one their fill's tone picks. color.text.* and the page's own borders and focus ring are the mode's own set, for the page's own surfaces. The harness checks every fill against what sits on it.

danger_apart.say: the primary and danger fills stay at least 10 apart (ΔE in OKLab, ×100) in every brand and mode
danger_apart.why: A destructive commit must never look like the everyday one.

neutral.description: The neutral scale (OD-228). Primitives hold the grays below, each a whole ramp in light and dark. color.neutral.<step> is a semantic scale: each scheme or brand points it at one gray, recorded in its theme as neutral { gray, temperature, why, because }. Surfaces, borders, text, the secondary button and disabled read only color.neutral steps, never a gray directly. A scheme keeps only the gray it picked; this list is the menu.

grays.description: A cool blue-gray, barely tinted: reads as precise.
A deeper, bluer gray, about twice as tinted as slate: cool and firm.
No hue at all: nothing can lower contrast or carry a meaning.
A warm, yellowish gray, like paper.
A warm, rosy gray that sits under a vivid brand.

catalogue.description: Every component a design system can carry: the UI components of the shadcn/ui registry (style new-york-v4, MIT), plus toast, which Open DS builds itself, data-table, which wraps TanStack Table after shadcn's Data Table guide, and date-picker, after shadcn's Date Picker. Each scheme picks its inventory from this list through the components scope. The component-api keys in components cover the ones built so far.

families.description: Buttons and toggles that start or switch something.
Fields, choices and pickers that take input.
Tables, charts and counts that show records.
Menus, tabs, breadcrumbs and bars that move between places.
Alerts, toasts, loading and empty states that report what happened.
Dialogs, sheets, popovers and tooltips that sit above the page.
Cards, separators and containers that group and arrange content.
Accordions and sections that organize long text.
Messages and attachments for chat interfaces.

A single section, not a stack.

items.not_when: A short confirmation that can go away by itself, or one notice for the whole site.

One full-width notice for the whole site.

variant.not_when: Something failed and must be fixed.

variant.apply_when: An error, with what went wrong and how to fix it.
variant.not_when: A plain note dressed as danger for emphasis.

accessibility.overview: An error that appears after an action is announced (role alert); a standing note is not.

items.not_when: Anything that can be undone (offer undo instead), or a form or task (use a dialog).

Undo after the fact, when the action can be reversed.

items.overview: A short label for a status, category or count, next to what it describes.

items.not_when: A message people must read (alert or toast), or an action (a button).

tone.overview: News: worth knowing, nothing to act on.
tone.not_when: Something is wrong or nearly wrong.
A state that is only waiting.

tone.overview: Needs attention soon; nothing has failed yet.
tone.apply_when: A risk people can still act on.

items.not_when: Comments on a page or long text (use a message or a card).

accessibility.overview: It stays a real table with headers; sorting and selection are announced.

keyboard.overview: Every tool and row action is reachable by keyboard.

items.description: A button that opens a calendar, for one date or a range. Built on calendar and popover, after shadcn's Date Picker.
items.overview: A field-like button that opens a calendar for one date or a range.
items.apply_when: Dates near today, ranges, or when the day of the week matters.
items.not_when: A date people know by heart, such as a birth date: typed fields are faster.

vs.why: The calendar on its own, always shown.

accessibility.overview: The button says the chosen date, not just Pick a date.

items.description: A window over the page for a focused task.
items.overview: A window over the page that takes attention until people finish or close it.
items.apply_when: People must decide or finish something before going back: a short form, an important choice.
items.not_when: A short status (toast), extra detail on the page (accordion), or a side panel that should not block the page (sheet).

vs.why: A side panel; the page stays in view.
Confirms something that cannot be undone.

accessibility.overview: It is a dialog with a title; the page behind is hidden from screen readers.
Focus moves in when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes.

keyboard.overview: Escape closes it.
Tab stays inside while it is open.

items.description: A panel that slides up from the bottom, for phones.
items.overview: A panel that slides up from the bottom, for phones.
items.apply_when: Filters, details or a short form on a phone, while the page stays partly in view.
items.not_when: A blocking decision (dialog), or a wide screen where a side panel fits better (sheet).

vs.why: Slides from an edge on wide screens.

accessibility.overview: It behaves as a dialog: named, focus moves in and back.

keyboard.overview: Escape closes it.

items.description: A menu of actions opened from a button.
items.overview: A menu of actions opened from a button.
items.apply_when: More actions than fit, or actions people use now and then.
items.not_when: Choosing a value for a field (select), or the one main action (a button).

accessibility.overview: The trigger says it opens a menu and whether it is open.

keyboard.overview: Arrows move; Enter runs; Escape closes and returns focus.

items.description: What to show when there is nothing yet.
items.overview: What a region shows when it loaded and has nothing: why, and what to do next.
items.apply_when: An empty list, a search with no results, or a first visit with no items yet.
items.not_when: Still loading (skeleton or spinner), or a load that failed (alert).

variant.overview: The picture shown as it is: an image or illustration.
variant.apply_when: A larger empty area where a picture helps.
variant.not_when: A small region where the picture would push the words away.

variant.overview: The picture as an icon in a small tile.
variant.apply_when: A compact empty state next to data.
variant.not_when: A first visit that needs more warmth than an icon.

items.description: A label, control, hint and error laid out together.
items.overview: A label, control, hint and error laid out together, the same way every time.
items.apply_when: Every form control that needs a label, a hint or an error.
items.not_when: A control that is not part of a form, such as a search box in a toolbar.

orientation.apply_when: Most forms: easy to scan from top to bottom.
orientation.not_when: Short settings where the label sits better beside.

orientation.apply_when: Settings and short controls such as switches.

orientation.overview: The label above on narrow screens and beside on wide ones.
orientation.apply_when: Forms people use on phones and laptops alike.
orientation.not_when: When one layout is simpler for everyone.

accessibility.overview: The label, hint and error are linked to the control, so they are read with it.

items.description: Form state and validation wired to fields.
items.overview: Form state and validation wired to the fields.
items.apply_when: Any form that checks answers and shows errors next to the fields.
items.not_when: A single control that saves at once (a switch).

vs.why: How one control is laid out.

accessibility.overview: Errors are announced, linked to their fields, and the first one gets focus on submit.

items.description: A preview card on hover.
items.overview: A preview card that appears on hover or focus.
items.apply_when: A quick look at a person or link for people with a mouse, with the same detail reachable on click.
items.not_when: The only way to see the content: touch screens have no hover.

vs.why: Opens on click, works on touch.

items.description: Single-line text entry.
items.overview: A labeled field for a short typed value.
items.apply_when: A name, email, phone number or other one-line answer.
items.not_when: Long text (textarea), or a closed choice (radio group, select or checkbox).

accessibility.overview: A visible label, never a placeholder as the only label.

items.description: An input with addons such as icons or buttons.
items.overview: An input with addons inside its border: icons, text, buttons.
items.apply_when: A search with an icon and a clear button, a value with a unit or currency.
items.not_when: Controls that are separate fields (lay them out with field).

align.overview: An addon before the text, on the same line: an icon or currency.
align.apply_when: A search icon or a unit that comes first.
align.not_when: Something people press often; put it after the text.

align.overview: An addon after the text: a unit, a clear button, a shortcut.
align.apply_when: Clear, submit or a unit that follows the value.
align.not_when: A label that should be outside the field.

align.overview: An addon row above the text, inside the field.
align.apply_when: A toolbar or a label row for a larger input.

align.overview: An addon row below the text, inside the field.
align.apply_when: A counter or actions under a larger input.

accessibility.overview: Addon buttons have names; icons that only decorate are hidden from screen readers.

items.description: Separate boxes for a one-time code.
items.overview: Separate boxes for a one-time code.
items.apply_when: A short code sent by text or email, typed or pasted.
items.not_when: Passwords or any value that is not a fixed-length code.

accessibility.overview: Screen readers hear one field with a label, and pasting the whole code works.

items.description: A row with media, title, description and actions.
items.overview: A row with media, a title, a description and actions.
items.apply_when: Lists of things such as people, files or settings, each with a few actions.
items.not_when: Records people compare cell by cell (a table).

vs.why: A larger unit with more content.

variant.overview: No border and no fill: the row sits on the surface around it.
variant.apply_when: Lists inside a card, panel or menu that already has a frame.
variant.not_when: Rows that stand alone on the page and need edges.

variant.apply_when: Rows that stand alone on the page, such as a list of settings.
variant.not_when: Long lists inside a framed panel, where borders add noise.

variant.overview: A soft fill behind the row.
variant.apply_when: A row that should stand out quietly, such as the current one.
variant.not_when: Every row in a long list.

size.not_when: Dense panels with many short rows.
Touch screens and lists people read slowly.

items.description: A keyboard key or shortcut.
items.overview: A keyboard key or shortcut, shown as text.
items.apply_when: Telling people the shortcut for an action.
items.not_when: Decoration, or the only way to discover an action.

items.description: The name of a form control.
items.overview: The visible name of a form control.
items.apply_when: Every form control.
items.not_when: Never skipped: a placeholder is not a label.

vs.why: The label laid out with hint and error.

accessibility.overview: The label is linked to its control and makes the hit area larger.

items.description: A divider or status line inside a conversation.
items.overview: A divider or status line inside a conversation, such as a date or someone joining.
items.apply_when: Breaking a long conversation into days or showing events in it.
items.not_when: A message someone wrote.

items.description: A row of menus, as in desktop apps.
items.overview: A row of menus, as in desktop apps.
items.apply_when: A dense desktop-style tool with many commands grouped by menu.
items.not_when: Website navigation (navigation menu), or phones.

keyboard.overview: Arrow keys move between and within menus; Escape closes.

items.description: One message with its author and time.
items.overview: One message with its author and time.
items.apply_when: Conversations, comments and activity feeds.
items.not_when: Status about the system (alert or toast).

items.description: A scrolling list of messages that keeps the newest in view.
items.overview: A scrolling list of messages that keeps the newest in view.
items.apply_when: A live conversation where new messages arrive at the bottom.
items.not_when: A static list (a scroll area).

accessibility.overview: New messages are announced politely without moving focus.

items.description: The browser select, styled.
items.overview: The browser's own select, styled.
items.apply_when: A plain closed list, especially on phones, where the system picker is best.
items.not_when: Options that need icons or rich content (select), or a short list better shown at once (radio group).

vs.why: A custom menu with richer options.
A short list shown at once.

items.description: Site navigation with links and panels.
items.overview: Site navigation with links and panels.
items.apply_when: The main sections of a website, sometimes with a panel of sub-links.
items.not_when: App navigation that stays open (sidebar), or actions (dropdown menu).

accessibility.overview: It is a navigation landmark; the current page is marked.

items.description: Moves between pages of results.
items.overview: Moves between pages of results.
items.apply_when: A list or table split across pages.
items.not_when: Steps of a task (progress).

accessibility.overview: The current page is marked; previous and next have names.

items.description: Rich content in a floating panel, opened by click.
items.overview: Rich content in a floating panel, opened by click.
items.apply_when: Extra detail or a small control next to what it explains, on any device.
items.not_when: A one-line hint (tooltip), or a task that should block the page (dialog).

accessibility.overview: The trigger says it opens a panel and whether it is open.

keyboard.overview: Escape closes it and returns focus.

items.description: How far a task has come.
items.overview: How far a task has come.
items.apply_when: A known amount of work: an upload, steps of a form.
items.not_when: A wait of unknown length (spinner), or a layout placeholder (skeleton).

accessibility.overview: It reports its value and has a name.

items.description: One choice from a short list.
items.overview: One choice from a short list shown at once.
items.apply_when: Two to about five options where the answer is one of them.
items.not_when: Many options (select), many answers (checkboxes), or a setting that applies at once (switch).

vs.why: More than one may be true.

accessibility.overview: The options are a group with a question as its name.

keyboard.overview: Arrow keys move the choice; Tab leaves the group.

items.description: Panels the user can resize by dragging.
items.overview: Panels people resize by dragging the line between them.
items.apply_when: Desktop tools where people choose how much space each panel gets.
items.not_when: Phones, or layouts with one obvious shape.

keyboard.overview: The handle can be focused and moved with arrow keys.

items.description: A region with styled scrollbars.
items.overview: A region with its own styled scrollbars.
items.apply_when: A fixed-height list or panel inside a larger page.
items.not_when: The whole page: let the page scroll.

vs.why: A conversation that keeps the newest in view.

keyboard.overview: The region can be focused and scrolled with the keyboard.

items.description: One choice from a list, in a menu.
items.overview: One choice from a list, in a menu.
items.apply_when: Four or more options, a known closed list, or a setting with a default.
items.not_when: Two to five options people should see (radio group), or many flags (checkboxes).

vs.why: A short list shown at once.
Type to find in a long list.

accessibility.overview: It has a visible label; the chosen value is announced.

keyboard.overview: Arrows move; Enter picks; Escape closes.

items.description: A line between groups.
items.overview: A line between groups.
items.apply_when: Separating groups that spacing alone does not separate.
items.not_when: Decoration between every item: spacing is quieter.

vs.why: A container, when groups need a boundary.

items.description: A panel that slides in from an edge.
items.overview: A panel that slides in from an edge.
items.apply_when: Filters, details or a secondary form while the page stays in view.
items.not_when: A blocking decision (dialog), or a tiny confirmation.

accessibility.overview: It behaves as a dialog: named, focus moves in and back.

keyboard.overview: Escape closes it.

items.description: The side navigation of an app.
items.overview: The side navigation of an app, open while people work.
items.apply_when: Apps with several sections people move between all session.
items.not_when: A website's main navigation (navigation menu), or a few sections that fit in tabs.

variant.overview: Menu items with no border; hover shows the item.
variant.apply_when: Most apps: quiet next to the content.
Items that need extra separation from a busy background.
variant.not_when: A quiet sidebar next to dense content.

size.overview: A taller row with room for an icon and two lines.
size.apply_when: A workspace or account switcher at the top.

accessibility.overview: It is a navigation landmark; the current section is marked; collapsing keeps names for icons.

items.description: A placeholder while content loads.
items.overview: Placeholder shapes that match the final layout, so the page does not jump when content arrives.
items.apply_when: Lists, cards, dashboards and tables whose shape is known.
items.not_when: A wait with no layout (spinner), or a region that loaded empty (empty).

accessibility.overview: The region says it is loading; the shapes themselves are hidden from screen readers.

items.description: A value picked by dragging along a track.
items.overview: A value picked by dragging along a track, when an exact number is not needed.
items.apply_when: Volume, brightness, a rough range; pair with a number field when precision matters.
items.not_when: An exact answer people must type.

accessibility.overview: It has a name and announces its value.

keyboard.overview: Arrow keys change the value; Home and End jump to the ends.

items.description: A small loading indicator.
items.overview: A small indicator that work is in progress when the time is unknown.
items.apply_when: Fetching a panel or syncing, a wait that is not the button itself.
items.not_when: A layout placeholder (skeleton), or known progress (progress).

accessibility.overview: It has a name such as Loading and is announced politely.

items.description: An on-off setting that applies at once.
items.overview: An on or off setting that applies at once, with no submit.
items.apply_when: A setting that should take effect as soon as it is flipped.
items.not_when: A choice that waits for a form (checkbox).

vs.why: A pressed button in a toolbar.

accessibility.overview: It is a switch with a visible label; on and off are announced.

keyboard.overview: Space flips it.

items.description: Rows and columns of records.
items.overview: Rows and columns of comparable records, with headers.
items.apply_when: Records people scan, sort or compare cell by cell.
items.not_when: A grid of teasers (cards), or the shape of a relationship (chart).

vs.why: Many records with search, filters and paging.

accessibility.overview: It has a caption and header cells, so each cell is read with its header.

items.description: Switches between views of the same thing.
items.overview: Switches between views of the same thing on one page.
items.apply_when: Related views of one object that people move between.
items.not_when: Navigation to other pages (links), or steps of a task (progress).

vs.why: Stacked sections people can open together.

accessibility.overview: It is a tablist; the selected tab owns its panel.

keyboard.overview: Arrow keys move between tabs; Tab moves into the panel.

items.description: Multi-line text entry.
items.overview: A field for free text over several lines.
items.apply_when: Comments, descriptions, anything longer than one line.
items.not_when: A one-line value (input), or a known set of options.

accessibility.overview: It has a visible label; a limit is announced as people type.

items.description: A short message that confirms an action and goes away.
items.overview: A short message that confirms an action and goes away.
items.apply_when: Saved, sent, exported: something people should notice without stopping.
items.not_when: A failure people must understand (alert or dialog), or a notice that stays (alert).

tone.overview: Confirms that something people care about worked.
tone.not_when: A routine change that needs no celebration.

tone.apply_when: What failed and how to fix it, when it can wait for people's attention.
tone.not_when: A failure that blocks the task: use an alert or a dialog.

accessibility.overview: It is announced politely without taking focus, and stays long enough to read.
Nothing people must act on lives only in a toast.

items.description: A button that stays pressed or not.
items.overview: A button that stays pressed or not.
items.apply_when: Turning a mode or format on and off in a toolbar, such as bold.
items.not_when: A setting saved at once (switch), or a one-off action (button).

variant.overview: No border; the pressed state shows as a fill.
variant.not_when: A toggle alone on a busy background.

variant.overview: A border, so the toggle reads as a control at rest.
variant.not_when: A dense toolbar of many toggles.

size.apply_when: A few toggles that need to be easy to hit.

accessibility.overview: It says whether it is pressed.

keyboard.overview: Space or Enter presses it.

items.description: A set of toggles where one or many stay pressed.
items.overview: A set of toggles where one or many stay pressed.
items.apply_when: Switching a view or a mode between a few options, such as list and grid.
items.not_when: A form answer (radio group), or actions (button group).

accessibility.overview: It is a group with a name; each toggle says whether it is pressed.

keyboard.overview: Arrow keys move between toggles.

items.description: A short hint on hover or focus.
items.overview: A short hint on hover or focus.
items.apply_when: A brief name or hint for a control that already has an accessible name.
items.not_when: The only place values or important words live, or touch screens, where hover never happens.

vs.why: Opens on click and works on touch.

accessibility.overview: It describes its trigger and also shows on keyboard focus.

keyboard.overview: Escape hides it.
